messages:
Jordan: Seeing a spike of 503s from edge cluster eu-west-2 when services try to talk to stateful pods. Noticing headless service DNS resolves to IPs but connections fail.
Maria: Which cluster and which svc? any patterns across nodes?
Jordan: cluster=edge-prod-2, svc=chunk-writer (headless). It's weird: `nslookup chunk-writer.default.svc.cluster.local` returns the pod IPs, but `curl` to <podIP>:8080 times out.
Devon: Can you `kubectl get endpoints chunk-writer -o yaml` and `kubectl get endpointslices -o wide`?
Jordan: Ran both, endpoints object is empty for the service but endpointSlices show the pod IPs across multiple slices. So Kube-proxy/iptables rules seem absent.
Sasha: That sounds like kube-proxy not translating endpointSlices into iptables rules. Which kube-proxy mode are we on? ipvs or iptables?
Jordan: iptables mode. Also noticing kube-proxy pods on several nodes are backoff-restarting around the time errors start.
Priya: Any relevant logs? paste the kube-proxy logs from one of the affected nodes.
Jordan: Pasted logs:
```
E0318 14:12:02.123456 1 proxier.go:1534] sync failed: failed to get endpoints for service default/chunk-writer: endpointslice API watch closed: unexpected EOF
E0318 14:12:02.123460 1 proxier.go:1540] failing next sync for node ip-10-2-9-7
```
Devon: Hmm watch closed errors. Could be API server connection drops or RBAC cache issues after the controller-manager churn. Any events on the nodes? `kubectl describe daemonset kube-proxy -n kube-system`?
Jordan: No recent changes in daemonset. Controller-manager had a failover event earlier when api-server leader rotated. But only for ~30s.
Maria: That could explain transient reconnections, but why endpoints object empty while endpointSlices populated? There is a conversion path in kube-proxy that translates slices -> endpoints for older components when necessary. If kube-proxy crashed mid-sync it might leave inconsistent iptables state.
Sasha: Also remember we had a known bug in kube-proxy v1.24 where a watch flurry causes worker queue to stall and skip endpoint syncs until restart. What version are we on?
Jordan: kube-proxy v1.24.3 on these nodes.
Priya: Quick mitigation - restart kube-proxy daemonset pods on affected nodes to force resync. Also can manually run `iptables-save` to confirm rules are missing for that svc port.
Devon: I agree. Rolling restart kube-proxy on nodes in small batches. Do we need a ticket to pin kube-proxy version or backport a patch?
Maria: Let's also redeploy the iptables rules by running `kubectl -n kube-system exec -it kube-proxy-... -- /usr/bin/kube-proxy --cleanup`? Not confident in that on prod. Restart safer.
Jordan: Rolling restart started. Restarting nodes: ip-10-2-9-7, ip-10-2-9-9 first.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-489 — svc-discovery-headless-eu-west-2. Pager duty notified.
Sasha: After restart, kube-proxy logs show successful endpoint slice processing and iptables rules were reapplied. Traffic restored on those nodes.
Jordan: Confirmed: `kubectl get endpoints chunk-writer` now shows pod IPs and `curl` is succeeding. Network SLOs back to normal.
Priya: Root cause hypothesis: kube-proxy v1.24.3 hitting watch/event storm from endpointSlice churn during a brief API server leader rotation — caused queue stall and missed endpoint syncs.
Devon: Action items: 1) Pin kube-proxy to v1.24.4+ with the patch, 2) add liveness probe on kube-proxy proxier sync loop to restart on stuck syncs, 3) run chaos test for API server leader flaps + endpoint churn, 4) postmortem.
Maria: I'll open the upgrade PR and add the liveness probe. Jordan, can you add timeline and logs to the incident ticket?
Jordan: Adding timeline and the logs now. Will schedule postmortem for tomorrow EOD. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: INC-2026-489 updated: mitigated -> monitoring."
